feed.title: State minimization in MuSig2 signing sessions

entry.title: State minimization in MuSig2 signing sessions
entry.summary:
The `psbt_session_id` mechanism has undergone significant changes in the Ledger Bitcoin app to improve functionality for MuSig2-based wallet accounts. Initially, the session identifier was generated by hashing sufficient transaction-specific information to ensure practical uniqueness. This approach, implemented since version 2.4.0 of the app, inadvertently prevented pre-generation of nonces for future transactions. As a result, an important user experience feature—managing multiple sessions or preparing ahead for transactions—was lost.
With the release of version 2.6.0, the application now derives the `session_id` based on two primary factors: the [BIP-388](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/9f3d3bc6a60db16efbdc71ac8f7ea30217fc0c39/bip-0388.mediawiki) wallet policy and, if available, additional entropy supplied via a proprietary global field in the PSBT called `MUSIG2_SESSION_ID`. The introduction of this additional entropy empowers software wallets to handle several parallel sessions for the same account, preventing collisions that would otherwise cause a new session to overwrite an existing one.
Despite these enhancements, some complexities persist in managing PSBT fields, particularly due to requirements outlined in [BIP-373](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/9f3d3bc6a60db16efbdc71ac8f7ea30217fc0c39/bip-0373.mediawiki). For example, the `PSBT_IN_MUSIG2_PUB_NONCE` field involves using the aggregate MuSig2 public key as part of the PSBT key for each input. Since future transaction inputs are typically unknown and may involve UTXOs at different addresses, this poses a challenge. Nevertheless, converting the PSBT keys for public nonces from an artificial PSBT used during Round 1 to those required in the actual PSBT for Round 2 is a straightforward process, unlikely to present significant difficulties for developers implementing these features.
